prompt.text:
Postav mi video, které vysvětluje pravidla sportu stylem televizní analýzy s AR grafikou. Bez AI video modelů a bez stahování assetů: 3D scénu, postavy, textury, grafiku i zvuk vytvoř kódem. Pracuj samostatně a průběžně mi ukazuj kontrolní snímky.

## Parametry (pro jiný sport změň tuhle sekci a sekci Scénář)
- Sport: fotbal
- Pravidla (9): ofsajd, faul, pokutový kop, vhazování, rohový kop + kop od branky, hra rukou, přímý volný kop, žlutá a červená karta, gól (celý míč za čarou)
- Jazyk všech textů: čeština (plná diakritika, desetinná čárka)
- Délka: cca 68 s (úvod ~4,5 s, každé pravidlo 6 až 8 s, závěr ~4 s)
- Formát: 1920×1080, 30 fps, MP4 (H.264 + AAC)
- Styl postav: PS2 éra ve stylu GTA San Andreas (low-poly tvarované tělo, ručně malované textury)
- Týmy: Červení (červený dres s bílými lemy, bílé trenky), Modří (královsky modrý dres, tmavě modré trenky), rozhodčí černý s limetkovými lemy, brankáři zelený a fialový

## Technologie a pipeline
- Three.js (npm). index.html obsahuje WebGL canvas 1920×1080 a nad ním DOM vrstvu pro HUD.
- Deterministická funkce `window.renderFrame(t)`: stav scény i HUD je čistá funkce času, žádný stav mezi snímky.
- `render.mjs`: lokální statický HTTP server + puppeteer-core se systémovým Chrome (headless, na Macu `--use-angle=metal`). Pro každý snímek zavolej renderFrame(t), počkej 2× requestAnimationFrame, udělej JPEG screenshot a pošli ho rourou do ffmpeg (libx264, CRF 18, yuv420p). Režimy: `stills t1 t2 …` (PNG na kontrolu), `video`, `info` (zapíše časovou osu do out/timeline.json).
- Cesty řeš přes fileURLToPath (složky s mezerami v názvu).
- WebGLRenderer s `preserveDrawingBuffer: true`, ACES tone mapping, PCF soft shadows. EffectComposer s MSAA (samples 4, HalfFloat): RenderPass, UnrealBloomPass, vlastní grade pass (vinětace, jemné zrno, chromatická aberace, záblesk, whip blur, VHS efekt), OutputPass.
- Zvuk: Python (numpy + scipy) syntetizuje celý soundtrack do WAV, ffmpeg ho přimíchá (AAC 192k).
- Výstupy: plná kvalita + webová verze (CRF 23 až 24, maxrate 10M).

## Struktura projektu
src/util.js (easing, tmap pro freeze a zpomalení, track() pro pohyb hráčů po časovaných waypointech s fází běhu podle uražené vzdálenosti, seeded rng), src/world.js, src/player.js, src/ar.js, src/hud.js, src/grade.js, src/segments.js, src/main.js, render.mjs, https://audio.py/, PROGRESS.md (průběžně zapisuj, co je hotové a jak se to pouští, ať se dá navázat po přerušení).

## Svět
- Hřiště 105×68 m. Tráva jako canvas textura (pruhy po 5,25 m, šum, skvrny) + dlaždicová detail textura přes onBeforeCompile. Čáry jako ostrá geometrie, ne textura. Vnější hrana čar = hranice hřiště.
- Branky se sítí (LineSegments), rohové praporky.
- Stadion: dvoupatrová mísa podle superelipsy, dav jako canvas textura lidí v řadách, LED pás mezi patry, střecha s žebry, řady reflektorů na hraně střechy (emisivní, bloom), vnější fasáda s osvětlenými okny, noční obloha, světla města kolem, tmavá zem.
- LED mantinely kolem hřiště s českými nápisy (PRAVIDLA FOTBALU, RESPEKT, FAIR PLAY, ZNEJ PRAVIDLA, #PRAVIDLAFOTBALU), pomalu se posouvají.
- Světla: 4 směrová světla z rohů střechy se stíny (shadow kamera zaostřená na akci daného segmentu), hemisférické světlo, jemná mlha.
- Analytický grade: do všech materiálů světa vlož přes onBeforeCompile sdílený uniform uFreeze (odbarvení do chladné šedozelené + ztmavení). AR materiály ho nemají, takže při zastaveném obrazu zůstanou syté.

## Postavy (styl GTA San Andreas)
- Hierarchický rig: root → body (pánev) → trup → hlava a ramena → lokty, kyčle → kolena → kotníky. Póza = sada úhlů (náklon a rotace trupu, flexe a abdukce ramen, lokty, kyčle, kolena, kotníky, náklon těla, výskok).
- Geometrie: trup jako LatheGeometry (široká ramena, užší pas), zúžené končetiny, klouby jako koule, dlaň s palcem, kopačka s podrážkou a zúženou špičkou, tvarovaná hlava (užší brada), nos, uši, vlasy jako slupka (krátké, objemné, ježek, holá hlava).
- Ručně malované canvas textury: obličej (oči s duhovkou a odleskem, obočí, stín nosu, rty, tváře, strniště nebo vousy, vlasová linie), dres (V-výstřih, boční pruhy, znak, sponzor, jméno a velké číslo na zádech, vrásky látky), rukávy, trenky s číslem, štulpny s pruhy.
- Každý hráč jiný: pleť, vlasy, účes, oči, vousy, barva kopaček, postava. Česká jména na zádech (NOVÁK, DVOŘÁK, RŮŽIČKA…).
- Procedurální běh (fáze z uražené vzdálenosti, ať nohy nekloužou) + knihovna póz: kop (nápřah, úder, dokopnutí), skluz, zakopnutí a pád, vhazování, výskok s paží nad hlavou, zvednutá karta, postoj ve zdi, výskok zdi, robinzonáda brankáře, hlava dolů.
- Zvýraznění: obrysová slupka (inverted hull, tloušťka podle vzdálenosti od kamery), průsvitný hologram „ducha“ pro naznačení restartu, rozsvícení paže.

## AR grafika (additive blending, depthWrite false, kreslí se postupně přes progress)
GroundLine (zářící čára na zemi), Curtain (svislá rovina: ofsajd, branková a postranní čára), GroundRing (prstenec nebo disk s pulzem, čárkováním a výsečí, třeba kruh 9,15 m), Area (vyplněné území s okrajem a skenem), Trail (trubice trajektorie míče), GroundArrow (šipka s běžícími chevrony), Marker (zaměřovač kontaktu), Beam (světelný sloup), ScanGrid (skenovací mřížka), Segment3D (měřicí úsečky), Silhouette (válec obrysu těla).
Barvy: tyrkysová = měření, červená = přestupek, jantarová = míč a území, zelená = platné rozhodnutí.
DŮLEŽITÉ: shadery musí být NaN-safe (clamp UV, žádné pow ze záporného čísla). MSAA na hranách extrapoluje UV a NaN se v bloomu rozleje do černých bloků přes půl obrazu.

## HUD (DOM, styl sportovního přenosu)
- Logo vlevo nahoře „PRAVIDLA FOTBALU / AR ANALÝZA ZÁPASU“ + počítadlo „01 / 09“.
- Vpravo nahoře stav (ŽIVĚ, ZÁZNAM, ZPOMALENĚ ×0,6, STOP · AR, PŘETÁČENÍ ◀◀, KONEC ZÁPASU) a herní čas.
- Lower third vlevo dole: číslo pravidla, název, jednověté vysvětlení, ukazatel postupu z 9 dílků.
- Panel rozhodnutí vpravo dole v barvě rozhodnutí (OFSAJD, PENALTA, GÓL…) s podtitulkem.
- Při zastavení obrazu: záblesk, rohové závorky, štítek „ZASTAVENÝ OBRAZ · AR ANALÝZA“, krátký technický řádek dole.
- AR štítky ukotvené na 3D bod (projekce kamerou) s odkazovou čarou. Drž je v bezpečné zóně (ne pod spodní grafikou, ne pod logem) a nesmí se překrývat.
- Velká grafika karty (žlutá a červená) s důvody, úvodní titulek, závěr „TEĎ ZNÁŠ PRAVIDLA.“ s mřížkou 9 pravidel, stinger přechod (šikmé pruhy navy, tyrkysová, bílá + logo) na každém střihu.
- Čitelnost: minimální velikosti (název pravidla 66 px, popis 29 px, štítek 33 px + podtitulek 21 px, technický řádek 22 px). Text vždy na tmavém podkladu, krátké texty. Line-height aspoň 1,05, aby diakritika (Ž, Č, Ř) nebyla oříznutá. Titulky neodhaluj maskou, vypadá to jako ořez: použij fade + rozostření + lehký zoom.
- Fonty: systémové s českou diakritikou (na macOS DIN Condensed + Avenir Next Condensed). Pokrytí znaků ověř předem přes fc-query.

## Scénář (vnitřní časy segmentů, natažení na čtení viz další sekce)
Úvod (3,5 s): dron sjíždí z noční oblohy přes střechu do stadionu na široký záběr středu hřiště. Skenovací mřížka přejede hřiště, pod hráči naskočí kroužky, štítek „MÍČ SLEDOVÁN“. Titulek „PRAVIDLA FOTBALU“, nad ním „TV ANALÝZA PRAVIDEL“, pod ním „9 KLÍČOVÝCH PRAVIDEL · AR ANALÝZA“.
1. Ofsajd: televizní kamera, Červený #8 přihrává, zastavení v okamžiku přihrávky. Kamera se přesune do osy ofsajdové linie. Tyrkysová rovina u nejzazší části těla předposledního obránce (Modrý #4), červená u předsunutého kolena útočníka (Červený #9), měření „+1,59 m“ (spočítej z kloubů, paže se nepočítají). Rozhodnutí OFSAJD: nepřímý volný kop, Modří.
2. Faul: záznam ×0,6 nízko u trávníku. Modrý #10 vede míč, Červený #6 jde skluzem zezadu do kotníku. Zastavení v okamžiku kontaktu: zaměřovač „KONTAKT“, „MÍSTO FAULU“ (kruh + sloup), šipka dráhy skluzu, červený obrys. Kamera obkrouží, pak pád. FAUL: přímý volný kop.
3. Penalta: Červený #9 ve vápně, Modrý #3 ho podrazí. Zastavení, jeřáb nahoru. Zvýraznění pokutového území, oblouk z místa faulu na pokutovou značku s drátěným míčem, „11 m“. PENALTA.
4. Vhazování: přihrávka Červeného #2 přejede postranní čáru (trajektorie se kreslí živě). Zastavení až ve chvíli, kdy je celý míč venku, střih na kameru za čarou. Červená rovina, „+15 cm“, „CELÝ MÍČ VENKU“, „POSLEDNÍ DOTEK · ČERVENÝ #2“, modrá šipka do hřiště a hologram modrého hráče s míčem nad hlavou. VHAZOVÁNÍ (Modří).
5. Roh + kop od branky: střela Červeného #10 tečovaná Modrým #4 za brankovou čáru → ROHOVÝ KOP. Pak efekt přetáčení (VHS) a stejná střela bez teče → KOP OD BRANKY (zvýrazněné brankové území).
6. Hra rukou: střela, Modrý #5 ve výskoku s paží nad ramenem, míč do předloktí. Paže zčervená, ramenní linie, čára paže „ÚHEL PAŽE 135°“, průsvitný válec „OBRYS TĚLA“. RUKA: přímý volný kop.
7. Volný kop: zeď na 8,00 m „ZEĎ MOC BLÍZKO“, nakreslí se kruh 9,15 m, zeď ustoupí, číslo naběhne na 9,15 m a zezelená. Kamera za exekutora, zahraný oblouk přes zeď zpomaleně, zastavení „PŘES ZEĎ“. PŘÍMÝ VOLNÝ KOP.
8. Karty: detail rozhodčího se žlutou kartou proti hráči se svěšenou hlavou + velká grafika ŽLUTÁ KARTA / NAPOMENUTÍ se 3 důvody. Střih, červená karta, vyloučený odchází + ČERVENÁ KARTA / VYLOUČENÍ.
9. Gól: střela, brankář vyrazí, míč padá na čáru. Kamera u brankové čáry. První zastavení: polovina míče na čáře, červená rovina, „−11 cm“, „ZATÍM NENÍ GÓL“. Míč se dokutálí. Druhé zastavení: celý míč za čarou, rovina zezelená, „+3 cm“, blesky foťáků v hledišti. GÓL.
Závěr (2,5 s): kamera stoupá nad hřiště (návrat k úvodnímu záběru), mřížka, „TEĎ ZNÁŠ PRAVIDLA.“ + mřížka 9 pravidel, stmívačka.

Každé zastavení obrazu: krátký záblesk, odbarvení scény, kamera se dál pomalu hýbe kolem zmrazených hráčů, AR prvky naskakují postupně. Mezi segmenty vždy stinger.

## Čas na čtení
Akce (běh, kopy, skluzy) běží ve skutečné rychlosti. Analytické části každého segmentu natáhni 1,5× až 2,1× přes warp funkci (výstupní čas → vnitřní čas segmentu), aby každé pravidlo bylo na obrazovce 6 až 8 s a všechny texty se daly v klidu přečíst. `node render.mjs info` exportuje výslednou časovou osu do out/timeline.json.

## Zvuk (procedurální, https://audio.py/)
120 BPM broadcast groove (kopák, virbl, hi-haty, basa se sidechainem, arpeggio, pad), riser v úvodu, závěrečný akord. Při zastaveném obrazu hudba ztlumená low-passem. Dav (filtrovaný šum s vlněním, řev při gólu), whoosh + boom na každém střihu, kovový úder na každém zastavení, krátké „razítko“ při rozhodnutí, píšťalka, kopy do míče, zvuk přetáčení. Časy všech zvuků načti z out/timeline.json, ať sedí na obraz i po změně délky. Cílová hlasitost kolem −14 LUFS.

## Postup práce a kontrola
1. Nejdřív rozjeď pipeline (server, render, ffmpeg) s jednou scénou a ověř, že WebGL v headless Chrome běží.
2. Po každé změně vyrenderuj kontrolní snímky v klíčových časech a prohlédni je, včetně výřezů na 100 % kvůli textu a diakritice.
3. Celé video kontroluj přes kontaktní listy (ffmpeg filtr tile) a snímky kolem přechodů.
4. Hotové video ověř dekódováním (`ffmpeg -v error -i video.mp4 -f null -`) a délku a stopy přes ffprobe.
5. Do PROGRESS.md průběžně zapisuj, co je hotové a jakými příkazy se to pouští.

prompt.text: MVの0:43〜46の動きを再現して欲しいのでもっと研究してください。 その上で、 実装 → 実際にゲームを起動 → プレイ → スクリーンショット確認 → 厳格なVisual QA → 改善 を繰り返してください。 評価は非常に厳しくしてください。「デモだから十分」「動くからOK」と判断してはいけません。Steamで販売されている高品質なインディーRPGと並べても見劣りしないレベルを目標にしてください。 必要に応じてベンチマークとなるゲーム（ロックマン11、プレイ動画：https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=Uc8Y_0kQ1ho）を調査し、情報密度、色彩、キャラクターの視認性、マップ、UI、アニメーション、戦闘演出を評価してください。ただし素材やデザインをコピーしてはいけません。 プレースホルダー、絵文字、単純な色付き四角形、未実装ボタン、TODOを最終成果物に残さないでください。 最優先するのはゲームの規模ではなく完成度です。 「技術デモ」ではなく、「この続きを遊びたいと思える市販インディーRPGの体験版」に見えるまで改善を続けてください。 ultracodeやサブエージェントなど利用可能な高性能な開発機能があれば積極的に使用してください。

summary.en: The creator compared Claude Opus 5.5 and ChatGPT-6 Astra on the same detailed prompt to build an interactive Arctic diorama in a single HTML file with native WebGPU, preferring Opus's visuals and colors.

prompt.text:
Create "Frostbay." — an interactive miniature Arctic diorama as ONE self-contained HTML file using native WebGPU (WGSL). Everything procedural: no libraries, no imported models, no image textures, no network requests.

SCENE
- A clear rectangular block of cold sea (≈10 × 7 units, ~1.6 deep) resting on a thick, glossy jelly foundation with rounded edges and soft layered bands of icy blue and pale lavender.
- A snowy rock island toward the back: wet dark rock at the tide line, a cut "core-sample" cross-section where it meets the glass, a few rounded boulders on the sea floor.
- An igloo built from individual curved snow blocks (rows offset like brickwork), a block entrance tunnel, a warm amber ice window and a glowing interior.
- A wooden plank pier on posts with a hanging lantern; a fluttering red-and-white flag on a pole.
- An orange kayak with a double-bladed paddle; ~10 irregular ice floes; a larger ice raft.
- Two harbour seals (spotted, pale muzzle): one basking on a shore ledge of the island, one lying on the raft.
- A humpback whale: one smooth continuous lofted body, pale throat pleats and belly, mouth line, eyes, knobbly rostrum, very long pale flippers, small dorsal fin, wide flukes.
- Calm editorial backdrop; the diorama casts a soft shadow on an unseen floor.

WATER (a real simulation, not a shader trick)
- Height-field long-wave sim (∂²h/∂t² = ∇·(g·depth ∇h)) on a ~200×140 grid, flux form (volume-conserving), fixed 180 Hz substeps, damping + light viscosity + hard clamps: stable at every slider setting and during frantic drags.
- Waves slow and steepen over the shallows, wrap around the island, reflect off the glass and settle.
- Press = a soft plunger making a deep hollow with a raised, volume-neutral rim; dragging sweeps it (speed-limited) and leaves real 3D wakes. Hover never makes waves. Touch supported.
- Dragging a glass side tilts and slides the block on its jelly (damped springs that wobble back) and the sea sloshes toward the new level; a local soft bulge follows the hand. Pulling a jelly edge stretches it locally, then it wobbles home.
- Floating things follow local height and averaged slope, drift, bump each other, avoid shallows and glass.

LIFE
- Kayak: draggable (with a wake). A strong local wave — high swing AND steep averaged slope across the hull — rolls it 180° and leaves it upside down; ordinary ripples and blizzard chop only rock it; never capsizes while held.
- Raft seal: breathes, looks around, articulated flippers. Strong waves make it lose balance, slip off head-first, fall in with a splash, then swim — head up, coordinated hind-flipper strokes, steering away from shallows and glass — and later hauls itself back onto the raft.
- Shore seal: breathes, gazes, scratches with a fore flipper, lifts its head when big waves come.
- Whale: its spine follows the path its head has swum, so it always moves head-first and bends through turns, never sliding backward. "Call the whale" (button or double-click / double-tap) brings it up to the surface, it blows a misty spout, its back heaves the water, then it dives with the flukes rolling under.

LOOK
- Opaque pass to HDR with 4× MSAA plus a distance buffer; water pass with screen-space refraction (wave-driven), depth absorption (deep cold blue, no tropical turquoise), Fresnel sky reflection, restrained soft highlights, foam on crests and shallows, side walls showing the underwater cross-section with a crisp waterline and total internal reflection.
- Moving caustics on everything under the surface, focused by the live wave curvature; soft key-light shadows; neutral tone mapping.
- Modes: Daylight, Snowfall (overcast, falling snow), Aurora night (green/violet curtains, twinkling stars, warm igloo and lantern light with reflections on the water). Blizzard toggle: dense wind-driven snow, gusts and chop on the sea.

UI
- Restrained editorial layout: large italic serif "Frostbay.", short atmospheric subtitle, live status pill, compact panel (weather segments, blizzard switch, jelly firmness, wave damping, tide, Call the whale, Pause, Reset, Camera), concise hints, readouts for seal, kayak, whale and swell; orbit and zoom (pinch on touch).
- Pause freezes all motion; Reset restores sea, block, raft seal and upright kayak.
- Mobile: stacked layout, collapsible controls, ≥44 px touch targets. Clear fallback card if WebGPU is unavailable.

Test water interaction, stability, animals, kayak drag and capsize, whale call, weather modes, pause/reset, shader compilation and mobile layout. Return the finished HTML only.

prompt.text:
【題材：金閣寺】のCADデータと、それを元にしたBlender動画を作って。

■ CADデータ
- 【題材】をイメージした配置図・平面図・立面図をDXFで作図（単位mm、表題欄つき）
- 3Dモデル（OBJ/STL/3D DXF）は不要

■ 動画（Blender 4.2、1920×1080、24fps、約20秒）
1. 冒頭：和紙の巻物が上から広がり、墨で描かれた配置図が現れる（題字・落款つき）
2. 図面の線が墨のワイヤーフレームとして立体に立ち上がる
3. 基壇→柱→壁→屋根→装飾の順に肉付けされ、線は実体に吸収されて消える
4. 完成したら巻物が消え、周りが【環境：例 紅葉の山と池／雪景色／海中】だとわかる演出
5. 最後にタイトル【題材名】を表示

■ 描写（リアル寄り）
- 樹木・植物は、枝ぶりと葉の1枚1枚が見える作りに（球の塊にしない）
- 遠景の山や森は木を密に並べ、空気遠近の霞をかける
- 空は物理的な空。時間帯は夕方の低い日差しで、影を長く
- 水面の映り込み、苔・岩・落ち葉など地面の細部も作る
- 建物は題材に合わせた細部（例：垂木・軒付・格子）まで
- テクスチャはプロシージャルで（朱漆・瓦・石・金など、題材に合わせて）
- 金属や金箔は白飛びさせず、素材の色が出るように
- 外観の参考画像：【画像を添付】

■ 音
- 外部素材なしでPython合成。場面の切り替わりに合わせた和風BGM＋効果音

■ 進め方
- テスト静止画を確認してから本番レンダリング
- 完成したらMP4で送って

title.zh: 像素风篮球游戏

summary.zh: 一个单页 HTML 像素风3D篮球比赛模拟，由 Sonnet 5.5 用 three.js 构建。比赛自动进行，包含攻防AI、球体物理、犯规、换人、回放和合成音效，耗时1小时35分钟，花费48.31美元。
summary.en: A self-playing pixel-art 3D basketball simulation in a single HTML page, built by Sonnet 5.5 with three.js. It has AI teams, ball physics, fouls, substitutions, replays and synthesised audio; it took 1 hour 35 minutes and cost $48.31.

prompt.text:
Build "Lamplight Classic": a single self-contained HTML page (no build step needed to run; one <title>, inline CSS/JS, only three.js r128 from cdnjs and Google Fonts allowed) that simulates a 5-on-5 basketball Grand Final as a pixel-art 3D diorama. The match plays itself; the viewer coaches and watches.

SETTING
Fictional "Brightwater Arena" on a floating island: indoor hall with stands (~1200 seats, ~1100 animated fans, two mascots), scoreboard video screen, scorer's table, benches, tunnel, plus an outside plaza (ticket booth, coffee cart, bus, street court, lamps). Four fictional teams, 12 named players each, unique first/last names per league. Women's league: Cedar Falls Magpies vs Redstone Stags. Men's league: Ironbridge Wolves vs Copperfield Falcons.

RENDERING
- Orthographic camera, 31 degree elevation, 45 degree azimuth, quarter-turn rotation, zoom, drag to orbit.
- Render to a low-res target with NearestFilter; one art pixel = 1-6 CSS px (slider, default 2).
- Depth-based outlines, fixed 90-colour OKLab palette quantisation, Bayer dithering.
- Custom lit material with 12 dynamic light slots (corner columns, flash/replay, hall glow, photographer flashes).
- People are instanced box-rigs (about 30 parts each, cap 64) with a pose system: dribble, shoot, pass, jump, block, rebound, celebrate, sit.
- "Doll's-house" cutaway: the near E/S walls lift so the court is never hidden.
- Three floors (Hardwood, Blue, Orange; each changes bounce and squeak), three lightings (Day, Evening, Show).
- Cameras: TV follow, Whole hall, Close-up, free. Show mode must not blow out.

WORLD AND PHYSICS
Metres, +x east, +z south. Court 28x15 (long axis z), rims at z=+/-12.425, rim height 3.05, three-point arc 6.75. Ball physics with real rim, backboard and net interaction, deterministic given a seed. Fixed 1/60 s step with accumulator, speed 0.5x-4x plus turbo. Two seeded RNGs: scenery and gameplay.

GAME AI (separate modules, clean ownership by possession phase)
- BK (body kinematics): timed actions, reach limits; dunks only when fingertips reach the rim (about 1 of 24 women, 8 of 24 men).
- PLAY (offence): ball handler, set plays and scripts, jump ball, inbounds, free throws, fast breaks.
- DEF (defence): man and zone, press, traps, rebounding, steals, blocks, contact, charges and fouls.
- Shared steering layer, A* navigation grid, event bus for handshakes (shotPressure, gain, foulCommit).
- BALL owns the ball (give, drive, hit, release, basket detection).
- Targets per team per 40 game-min: about 75-85 points, FG 42-48%, 3PA share 30-40%, 6-9 steals, 3-5 blocks, 17-22 fouls, 13 turnovers, 25-32% offensive rebounds.

RULES AND FLOW (coroutine-based match scheduler)
FIBA-style: 24 s shot clock, team fouls and bonus, free throws, throw-ins, possession arrow, 3-second rule, 8-second rule, substitutions (automatic and requested), timeouts, overtime. Game clock runs 2x. Formats: Quick 4x2:00, Standard 4x5:00, Full 4x10:00, Best of 3 (4x3:00). Coach's challenge with video review, instant replay of baskets from a ring buffer, ceremonies (walk-on, anthem, warm-up, handshakes, trophy), commentary lines, full box score and team stats that must reconcile (score = period scores = team stats = player points).

UI
Panel beside the stage (stacked under it on phones, scoreboard sticky on top). Sections: Match (league, format, teams, new match, skip ceremony), Hall (floor, lights, light columns), Coach (offence: push the pace, run sets, pick and roll; defence; Feed him; timeout; substitutions), View (camera, pixel size), live stats, play-by-play log. Keyboard shortcuts for rotate, camera, pause, new match, skip, timeout. Scoreboard bug: period, game clock, 24 s clock, per-team fouls, bonus, timeouts, possession arrow.
Visual identity: "programme of a night game", cream paper and charcoal ink, signal orange and lamp yellow, Big Shoulders Display + Hanken Grotesk, light and dark themes. English UI.

AUDIO
No audio files: synthesise everything in WebAudio (crowd murmur and roars, whistle, buzzer, rim, net, sneaker squeaks, ball bounce, anthem). Start from a button, with a mute toggle.

QUALITY BAR
- The first match after page load must play exactly like "New match".
- Headless whole-game tests across all formats and both leagues: no console errors, no negative or NaN clocks, no rule-violation events, reconciled stats.
- Screenshot QA at four camera quarter-turns, three lightings, three floors and a 390x844 phone viewport; no horizontal scroll.
- Keep sim+view under about 3 ms per 1/60 s step on a software renderer.

DELIVERY
Write a short module contract first (public API per module), then build modules in parallel if you can: court and hoops, hall and stands, people and poses, ball physics, BK, PLAY, DEF, match flow, crowd and FX, audio, UI. Publish the page as an artifact and also give me a standalone .html file.

summary.en: A pixel-art 3D futsal school-yard diorama was built in separate Opus and Sonnet runs, with Three.js and a simulated match engine.

prompt.text:
Build a single-file pixel-art 3D diorama (three.js r160, orthographic camera at ~31°, rotatable in 90° steps, low-res render target with depth outlines and a quantized palette) of a futsal 5-a-side match on a small floating island: a school yard. Original content only, English UI.

Scene: a 40×20 m blue rubber futsal court inside a wire cage (cutaway on the sides nearest the camera), 3×2 m red-and-white goals, proper futsal markings (6 m arc areas, 6 m and 10 m spots, centre circle). Team benches and a timekeeper's table on one touchline, small bleachers on three sides with an instanced crowd of kids and parents. Behind the north end: a school facade ("School No. 12") with porch and door the teams walk out of, a wall clock with moving hands, a flag, and a 64×32 pixel scoreboard on the wall showing score, clock and team fouls. Around the court: playground, bike rack, shed, basketball hoop, snack kiosk, trees, ball boys, a photographer, stewards.

Match engine: 4 school clubs with distinct kits (none matching the court colour), 9-player squads (5 on court + 4 subs) in a 1-2-1 formation (GK, fixo, two alas, pivot). Two halves of 20 match minutes (real length selectable), no offside, kick-ins instead of throw-ins, keeper restarts by pass, corners and free kicks scaled to the small court. Ball physics with drag, analytic rolling and lob solving; short passing, shots from distance, rare crosses. Referee on one touchline, second official at the table. Coroutine-driven agents with A* navigation: walk-out from the school door, warm-up, kick-off, goal celebrations, half-time, full-time handshakes. Commentary feed, viewer actions (Shoot / Square it / Hit it long, click to mark the next pass), camera modes (TV follow, whole yard, close-up), day / dusk / night with four corner floodlights.

Switchable court surface (segmented control): rubber (blue), asphalt, artificial turf, wooden parquet. Each swaps the court texture AND the ball physics constants — rolling resistance, bounce restitution, skid — so asphalt is fast and bouncy, turf slows the ball and kills the bounce, parquet is the quickest and slickest.

Page: light editorial layout with a small mast, the canvas, and a control panel (match length, surface, time of day, views, commentary). Must work at phone width.

prompt.text: Make an interactive WebGPU soft-body study of a great hammerhead shark cast in two layers of jelly, resting on its belly in a soft photo studio. Build it from a signed distance field: an elliptical body section swept along the spine, slim at the neck, deep at the chest, with a slim caudal peduncle. Give it an oversized cephalofoil — a wide, flat hammer whose span is about 40% of the body length, with a nearly straight front edge, a small notch in the middle, ends swept slightly back, full and round at the front and thinning toward the back, with a large glossy eye at each tip. Seven kinds of fin from one recipe (convex leading edge, falcate trailing edge, thinning toward the tip): a very tall sickle-shaped first dorsal, second dorsal, pectorals, tall pelvic fins, anal fin and a lopsided tail with a subterminal notch. Clear tinted jelly over a milky white belly layer that also fills the underside of the hammer; trapped bubbles; a darker back, dusky fin tips, five gill slits, a small crescent mouth with milky teeth, grooves along the front of the hammer and pores beneath it, all drawn in the shader from rest-space coordinates so they stretch with the jelly. Simulate it as an XPBD tetrahedral mesh (snapped hex lattice, co-rotational elasticity, volume preservation, floor friction), with firmer fins. Muscle strain drives two moves: a slow head sweep from side to side, like a metal detector over the sand, and a tail swish. Let the user grab and stretch the jelly, twist with the scroll wheel or a second finger, drop beads of jelly bait, and switch between three colourways (steel, amber, gummy blue). Render with refraction, Beer–Lambert absorption, back-lit glow in the thin parts and tinted shadows. Show live mass, volume, fork length and the distance between the eyes.

A real-time three.js scene rendered small and quantised to a palette: a mountain shrine on a floating island at night in heavy rain (hall with vermilion pillars, torii gate, stone lanterns, koi pond, cedar, maple, bamboo). Six original swordsmen meet two at a time: arrival in straw hats, seconds with umbrellas, the drum, the bow, the draw; stances, cuts, parries, locked blades, and a final charge past each other in a lightning flash. Nobody dies — the loser is disarmed or has the hair cord cut, kneels and bows; the winner shakes off the rain and sheathes the blade. summary.zh: 用一份长篇详细提示词（明确禁止画面出现任何文字）做出一艘写实感十足、可交互的日落海盗船3D场景，并与Astra用同一提示词的结果做对比。
summary.en: A cinematic, interactive pirate-ship 3D scene on a sunset ocean, built from one long detailed prompt banning any on-screen text; compared against Astra's version of the same prompt.

prompt.text: Create from scratch a fully interactive 3D scene of a pirate ship sailing across a dynamic ocean at sunset. The visual style should be cinematic and stylized rather than photorealistic, while still being exceptionally rich, detailed, polished, and visually sophisticated. Build the ship, ocean, sky, lighting, materials, sails, rigging, cannons, small structural details, sea foam, wake, particles, animation, camera work, composition, atmospheric depth, and color grading. The final result should feel like a premium, high-production 3D artwork, not a prototype, technical demo, or low-quality scene. Start from a completely blank page. Do not reuse or depend on any previous project or scene. You may create the assets yourself or use reliable, trusted, open-source assets and libraries when necessary. Mandatory requirements: No text of any kind may appear anywhere inside the scene. No titles, names, logos, descriptions, credits, labels, or control instructions in any language. Deliver the entire project as one final standalone page file that can be opened directly in a web browser, with assets embedded inside it as much as reasonably possible. The ocean, ship, sails, and camera must all be animated naturally and smoothly. Avoid artificial slow motion or sluggish movement. The ship should feel like it is genuinely moving through the water. Do not rely on primitive geometric shapes as the finished result. Build a visually convincing and detailed pirate ship, including a carefully shaped hull, masts, sails, rigging, ropes, cannons, railings, lanterns, deck structures, and clearly visible small-scale details. Lighting must reveal the ship's geometry and materials clearly. Create a rich sunset atmosphere, deep ocean shading, reflections, convincing sea foam, and a detailed sailing wake behind and around the vessel. Maintain a strong balance between visual quality and real-time performance, preserving smooth interaction and animation without making an obvious sacrifice in quality. Automatically use the most appropriate skills, tools, libraries, techniques, and available assets needed to achieve the best result. Do not wait for me to specify which technologies to use. Actually test the finished result in a desktop web browser. Capture visual screenshots, inspect the browser console for errors, and fix every visible or technical issue you find, including distorted geometry, black screens, failed asset loading, broken animation, poor composition, rendering artifacts, or camera problems. At the end, verify that the final file opens and works directly, that the scene contains no text whatsoever, and that there are no remaining runtime or loading errors. Then finish the task with only a brief response.

It should take inspiration from the ingame map, the minecraft art style, as well as realistic old map parchments, and popular map animations on pinterest. i want the animation to appear by having it being lifted up into view on screen, and then the elements gradually appearing as if it's a hidden treasure map being revealed. i then want you to animate a route from the first location, and then to 4 other locations, starting at the first, and ending at the last. make the last location special by making it glow in gold to show that it's the final destination. title.zh: 互动锦鲤池同题对比

summary.zh: 作者用同一段详细提示词分别让Claude Opus 5.5和GPT-6 Astra制作了一个基于Three.js/WebGL的互动锦鲤池网页，并对比了两者效果。
summary.en: An interactive 3D koi pond web app built with Three.js/WebGL, created from a detailed prompt and compared side-by-side with a version made by GPT-6 Astra using the same prompt.

prompt.text:
Build a beautiful, full-screen interactive koi pond using Three.js + WebGL. Use a top-down view with clear turquoise water, sunlight, animated caustics on the pond floor, and a convincing sense of depth.

Place an elegant translucent selection panel at the bottom with four koi varieties: Kohaku, Showa, Golden Ogon, and Platinum. Clicking a card releases that fish into the pond. Dragging a fish from its card lets the user choose exactly where to drop it.

Make each landing feel satisfying: a splash with droplets, a brief depression in the water surface, and expanding ripples. The fish should then dive beneath the surface. Use refraction and depth cues so the koi clearly look submerged.

Create detailed 3D koi with eyes, scales, fins, and flowing tails. Animate their bodies, tails, and fins together. Each fish should independently change direction and speed, turn smoothly near boundaries, and avoid other fish.

Let users touch and drag across the water to create ripples. Add rain and a movable whirlpool whose current affects the fish. Include Calm, Clear pond, and a control to hide the interface for screen recording.

Use Web Audio to create landing splashes, soft musical droplets, gentle swimming water sounds, rain, and a whirlpool sound. Enable audio through a Sound button, fade it smoothly when muted, and pause it when the browser tab is hidden.

Keep all labels and buttons in English. Make the layout responsive for mobile. Optimize rendering and animation for smooth performance with several dozen fish.

Deliver a complete, working website with polished visuals and functional interactions.

title.zh: 运河风车3D场景模型对比
title.en: 3D canal and windmill scene model comparison

summary.zh: 作者用一段详细的WebGPU/WGSL提示词让Opus 5.5制作出一个带物理水面、船只和野生动物的果冻风格运河船闸互动场景，效果优于用同一任务测试的ChatGPT-6 Astra和Gemini 4 Argon。
summary.en: Using a detailed WebGPU/WGSL prompt, Opus 5.5 built an interactive jelly diorama of an English canal lock scene with physics-based water, boats and wildlife, outperforming ChatGPT-6 Astra and Gemini 4 Argon on the same task.

prompt.text:
Build "Lock Jelly." — a single self-contained HTML file (WebGPU + WGSL, no libraries, no network, works from file://), part of a "Material Studies" series of jelly dioramas. If WebGPU is missing or the adapter fails, show a clean fallback card instead of the scene.

CONCEPT
A square block of clear coloured jelly (about 5.2 × 5.2 units, ~2 units high) holding a little English canal scene. The canal runs along the FRONT edge of the block, so the block's front face cuts the water lengthways: you see the lock chamber in cross-section, the water inside it rising and falling between the gates, fish swimming, the boat's hull below the waterline. All cut faces show candy-coloured soil strata; under the pounds a blue-grey puddle-clay lining, under the chamber a brick invert on a concrete bed, under the fields brown earth and turf.

LAYOUT (left to right along the front)
- Upper pound on the left at the higher level, opening into a round winding hole (a bay for turning boats); near the lock it narrows between brick wing walls.
- The lock chamber in the middle: brick walls with dressed-stone quoins and coping, a slimy band between the two water levels and weed below, an iron ladder, a gauge board, a stone cill under the top gate, recesses that the open gates fold into.
- Below the bottom gate a short walled tail, then the lower pound bends away from the front face, runs under a humpback brick bridge into a basin with a willow-covered island, lily pads in its corners and a sunken bicycle on the bed.
- The ground steps down from an upper terrace to a lower one along a grassy bank.
- Behind the lock: stone setts around the chamber, bollards, a gravel towpath, a lane, the keeper's whitewashed cottage with a slate roof, green door, picket-fence garden full of flowers and washing flapping on a line, a gas lamp, a bench, a white windmill with turning lattice sails, oaks, willows, poplars, a hedge, sheep, reeds on the soft banks.

WATER
- Linear shallow-water waves on a staggered grid (~168²) with a little surface tension, so short ripples are springy like jelly; damping and firmness are adjustable.
- Three separate bodies of water — upper pound, chamber, lower pound — each with its own rest level. Faces between bodies stay shut unless the gate between them is open and the levels are equal. The chamber's level is moved bodily when paddles are drawn (Torricelli-style flow), with boils, white water and a dimple at the intake.
- Rendering: refraction of the scene behind, flavour-coloured absorption, sun caustics on the bed, soft light shafts, foam (wakes, paddle churn), a meniscus line on the cut faces. Split the surface mesh along the gate lines so the step in level at a shut gate is a clean wall hidden by the gate leaf, not a ramp.
- The block itself can be tipped by dragging its side; the jelly shears and wobbles, the water sloshes, and it settles back.

THE LOCK AND THE KEEPER
- Two single-leaf timber gates (planks, rails, diagonal brace, iron straps, a walkway with a handrail), each with a white balance beam with black bands. Ground-paddle pedestals with toothed racks that rise when wound.
- An articulated lock keeper (flat cap, navy jumper, cords, windlass in hand; torso, arms, thighs and shins as separate parts). He walks with a proper gait, plans his route around the bench, pedestals, bollards and any beam lying across his way (going round the beam's end), leans his back on a beam and walks it round backwards to swing a gate, winds the windlass with his arm circling the spindle, and sits on his bench between jobs. He sets off for the gate as the boat comes in.
- The cycle: the boat lies in the full chamber → keeper shuts the top gate → winds up the bottom paddles → the chamber empties into the tail with white water → winds them down → opens the bottom gate → the boat leaves, runs the tail, swings round the bend, ducks under the bridge, goes round the island and comes back into the chamber bow first → shut bottom gate → round to the top paddles → chamber fills with boils → open the top gate → the boat goes up the pound, turns in the winding hole and comes back. Repeat forever. A gate may only open when the levels match.

BOATS
- A traditional narrowboat "Wobble": black lofted hull, a green cabin with red lining-out, brass portholes, a cratch board and cover at the bow, a chimney with brass bands (puffing smoke), a painted Buckby can, plank and pole on the roof, rope fenders, a headlamp, a brass swan-neck tiller and a steerer in a red jumper. It follows smooth filleted routes (check the stern never swings out through the block's face), slows near the gates, heaves, pitches and rolls on the local surface, and hands its displaced volume back to the water so it makes bow waves and wakes.
- Three moored narrowboats in the basin in different liveries with flowerpots on the roofs and one ginger cat, tied to bank pins with stretchy mooring lines.

LIFE
- Roach, perch and bream as boids that stay in their own body of water (they can only move between pound and chamber while a gate is open), under the surface and hulls, off the bed, scattering from the boat and splashes.
- Mallards (drakes, ducks) and a duck with four ducklings that follow exactly along her trail; a pair of mute swans in the basin. They paddle the surface, ride the chamber down and up, upend now and then, get out of the boat's way and come for bread.
- A grey heron that wades in the shallows or stands on a moored boat's roof, stabs at fish (sometimes catching one), and flaps off somewhere quieter when the boat passes or someone toots.
- Chimney smoke from the boat and the cottage.

UI (editorial, like a print magazine)
- Top-left: small caps eyebrow "MATERIAL STUDIES", a huge italic serif title "Lock / Jelly.", a short subtitle. Top-right: a status pill "WebGPU · Live / Paused / Unavailable".
- Right: a frosted-glass control panel (a bottom sheet on mobile) with: buttons Hurry (speeds the keeper, paddles and boat), Toot (horn; also Space), Throw bread, Rubber duck (drops a yellow rubber duck that floats upright, can be picked up and thrown, rides the lock, is stopped by gates and shoved by boats); a liveliness meter; tallies Trips · Lockfuls · Fed; a status line "Wobble — Emptying the lock 62%" telling the story step by step; three flavours Greengage, Elderflower, Blackcurrant (change the water colour/absorption and strata); sliders Firmness, Wave damping, Paddle speed; Reset, Pause, Sound on/off, View.
- Bottom-left: "How to play — Throw bread. Toot the horn. Hurry the keeper." with a small line of instructions.
- Interaction: drag across the water to make waves, drag the block's side to tip it, pick up and throw rubber ducks, drag empty space to orbit, scroll/pinch to zoom; touch works.
- Soft studio lighting on a warm paper backdrop with the block's tinted, caustic-flecked shadow; WebAudio sounds: the boat's horn, the gate thudding shut, a creak, the windlass ratchet, and the rush of water that swells with the flow.

QUALITY
Keep it smooth (fixed-step physics, cheap per frame), no console errors, no page scroll, works at phone width. Test it headlessly: a full round trip happens, levels go exactly from upper to lower and back, no gate opens across a step, the keeper never walks into the water or through obstacles, the boat never touches a gate leaf, and every button works.

summary.en: Creator generated a photorealistic WebGPU soft-body kiwi jelly simulation as a single HTML file with Claude Opus 5.5, compared cost and quality against Claude Fable 5.1, and posted the full prompt in a reply.

prompt.text:
Build "Kiwi Jelly Wedge" — a single self-contained HTML file (inline JS/CSS, no libraries): a real-time WebGPU soft-body gummy kiwi wedge you can grab, stretch, lift and twist.
Object
One sixth of a thick kiwi slice: a pie-shaped wedge with 30° half-angle, radius ≈ 1.8 and thickness 0.56. Rounded corners (iq's exact pie SDF minus a rounding radius) and bevelled top/bottom edges.
Regions, measured from the tip in rest space:a cream core at the tip with a slightly lobed edge;
thin pale rays fanning out of the core every 2π/56, each with its own random brightness and length;
a darker, glassier ring around the seeds (blushes red in the Ruby variety);
bright juicy outer flesh with radial cell grain and a lighter band just under the skin;
a thin brown fuzzy skin on the arc wall.

Seeds:small flattened black teardrops, pointed end toward the core, in radial rows between the rays, at four depths;
the face layers break the cut surfaces like real seeds; the others float inside and show through the jelly;
wet glossy shading.

A few small air bubbles in the outer flesh.
Varieties: Green, Gold, Ruby.
Physics (XPBD tetrahedral soft body)
Mesh: 2D Delaunay of the rounded outline plus a hex lattice, extruded into prisms → tets.
Co-rotational per-tet shape matching (warm-started quaternion) plus volume constraints.
Stiffer skin and core tets; edge-velocity damping; floor contact with Coulomb friction.
Soft patch grab with bounded reach; scroll or a second finger twists the held patch.
Fixed 60 Hz step with 10 substeps; gentle settling.
Seeds and bubbles are separate meshes embedded in the tets by barycentric weights, so they ride with the flesh.
Rendering (WebGPU / WGSL)
Procedural photo-studio cyclorama with softboxes. Soft PCSS key shadow tinted green, plus contact AO from a top-down height map.
Seeds and bubbles are drawn in the scene pass. A back-face pass gives the view-ray thickness.
Jelly:refraction of the scene, with per-tap Beer–Lambert absorption by material (flesh, glassy seed ring, milky core and rays, opaque skin);
scattering, back-lit glow at thin edges, Fresnel studio reflections and GGX highlights;
a velvet sheen on the fuzzy skin;
sparse sugar glints in the flesh.

Post: exposure, Khronos PBR Neutral tone mapping, sRGB, dither.
UI (editorial "Material Studies / No. 028", English)
Italic serif title "Kiwi / Jelly." with the caption "An emerald wedge. A halo of seeds. A gentle wobble."
Status pill "WEBGPU · LIVE".
Panel "The Specimen": variety chips (skin / core / flesh bands); Firmness ("trembling → set") and Internal damping ("lively → syrupy") sliders; Give it a nudge, Reset, Pause; ¼ speed and Show mesh.
Readouts: Mass (g, 1 unit ≈ 1.6 cm at 1.3 g/cm³), Volume (% of rest), Kinetic (µJ).
A collapsible "Inside the experiment" with notes on the method.
Fallback "This kiwi needs WebGPU." Stacked mobile layout with no horizontal scroll.

summary.zh: 作者用Opus 5.5纯代码制作了一段24秒循环播放的产品发布视频，需要用户提供照片和歌曲素材，并公开了详细的结构化提示词和渲染流程作为模板。
summary.en: A 24-second looping product launch video rendered entirely from code with Opus 5.5, using user-supplied photos and a song, with the structured prompt and build/render instructions shared as an open-sourced template.

prompt.text:
<inputs>
Ask me for: my product's name (one lowercase word, it becomes a black wordmark with a period), the one job a user hands it before bed, the three results it reports by morning, two photos of the same place at night and by day (aligned, so a crossfade reads as a real sunrise), one sunny daytime photo for outside the logo, and a song with a big hit near its start. If I skip any, use the defaults: "nightshift", "book 10 sales calls this week", 200 leads found / 200 emails sent / 10 calls booked.
</inputs>

<direction>
A 24 second square product launch video, 1440x1440 at 60fps, 2D only, one continuous take that loops. The whole video happens inside the period of the wordmark. Outside it's daytime (the sunny photo behind a black wordmark). Inside it's the night photo under iOS-style glass panels (the blurred photo behind each panel, a tint, a rim light). Nothing cuts: every scene grows out of the last, shapes morph, dots fly, colours change under floods. Every morph glides 0.8s on cubic-bezier(.45,0,.15,1) and the camera zoom rides the same curve. Geist, the real macOS pointer, soft shadows that grow with each shape's height.
Banned: flat or gradient backgrounds made in code, camera zooms into tiny points, hard cuts, crossfades between scenes, bouncy springs, particles, glows, holds longer than 1s, cropped type.
</direction>

<structure>
Beats are the song's. The song enters on its big hit as the first pill appears.
Open: the letters slide into the period and vanish into it while it glides to the middle. The period opens like an iris onto the night inside it, and "you log off at 6", then "[product] doesn't", roll through one mask line over the night photo.
Ask: a glass "Ask [product]" pill springs in. The cursor clicks it, it glides into an input and the job types out.
Find: send shrinks the input to a dot that ripples into a 23x15 grid. A scan line sweeps it, 200 dots light up and a counter counts them.
Write: the lit dots pour into a glass email composer. A second, purple cursor labelled "[product]" types a personal opener and presses Send, and the counter runs to 200/200.
Night: the composer becomes a glass orb with a progress ring. A clock chip swaps 11:42 PM, 3:17 AM, 5:02 AM, 6:59 AM while the sky relights from night to dawn and "while you sleep" rolls in.
Results (beat 20): the orb turns black and goo-splits into the three result pills. The checks pop green.
Morning: the pills merge into a Dynamic Island that grows into a phone lock screen: the day photo, the date, a big 7:00, the bezel growing out of the screen edge. Three glass notifications stack in, and the cursor taps the first, which opens like iOS.
Proof: a week calendar (10 meetings pop in, a hover shows one's time), then a pipeline chart ($48,200 counts up, the line draws, a hover follows it). A black flood from the line's end becomes "Start your night shift →" and the cursor clicks it.
Out: the button shrinks into a dot, the whole scene closes down into it like an iris, and the letters slide back out of the period. The tagline rises. Last frame = first frame.
</structure>

<build>
1. One HTML canvas. Everything is a pure function of time inside seek(t): no timers, no state between frames.
2. One element morphs through every state (size, radius, colour, material) from a table of beat times, so retiming is one edit.
3. Render the inside world into an offscreen canvas and reveal it through the period with a circular mask. Never zoom the camera into the dot.
4. Glass: a pre-blurred copy of the photo clipped to the shape, then a tint and a gradient rim.
5. Goo: blur + alpha threshold on an offscreen layer for the split and the merge.
6. Sound: a downloaded SFX for every event, each placed by its measured peak. The song enters on its hit. Loudnorm to -14 LUFS.
7. Render with Playwright at 60fps with 4 motion-blur subframes. Scan every frame for single-frame jumps and fix each one.
</build>

<gotchas>
A camera zoom into an off-centre dot swings sideways and spikes, so open the dot instead. Ease a closing iris by area, not radius, or its first frames jump. A helper that sets globalAlpha must restore the caller's, or fading cards pop. Counters read the frame's time, not the subframe's, or the digits smear.
</gotchas>

<start>
Ask me for the inputs, then show me the beat map and 6 stills (open, find, write, results, phone, out) before you render.
</start>

summary.en: A browser-based WebGPU jelly peach simulation with squishable flesh and a poppable pit, built with Claude Opus 5.5 for $7.11; the full build prompt was posted in the thread.

prompt.text:
Build a single-file WebGPU page "Peach Jelly" in the style of a "Material Studies" specimen sheet (light studio backdrop #E2DFDA, italic serif title, a specimen control panel on the right, live readouts bottom-left, collapsible "Inside the experiment" notes; responsive with a stacked phone layout and a no-WebGPU fallback card).

Subject: half a peach made of translucent jelly, cut along its suture, lying skin-down with the cut face up and its stone seated in the hollow.

Geometry: a signed distance field for the fruit — a sphere slightly longer from stem to blossom end, with a stem dimple, a faint point at the blossom tip and the suture crease along one side of the rim, belly gently flattened on the floor — cut at the equator, minus an almond-shaped hollow for the stone (flattened, broad faces parallel to the cut, blunt toward the stem). Simulation mesh: a snapped hex lattice, 5 tets per cell (~700 particles / ~2500 tets), node layers exactly on the floor and the cut face, nodes forced out of the stone. Render surface by surface nets, embedded in the tets by barycentric weights, with one normal-smoothing pass per frame so reflections don't pick out tet kinks. The stone gets its own high-resolution mesh: deep wormy furrows (mostly lengthwise) and little pits carved by displacement, a low keel round its edge, a small point at the blossom end; groove depth rides in the vertex material id for shading.

Physics (CPU, XPBD, 60 Hz, 10 substeps): per-tet co-rotational shape matching + volume constraints, stiffer skin, edge-relative damping, floor friction, pointer grab with twist. The stone is a rigid body (position, quaternion, ellipsoid inertia) with frictional contact against every particle and sampled floor contacts. Nodes lining the hollow are held by soft adhesion bonds that peel (floor of the hollow first, lip last) under a sustained net pull measured in the half's best-fit rigid frame — never from brief knocks; a loose stone resting in the hollow is drawn home and re-bonded with a soft grace period. Grabbing the stone moves it as a whole and it can be thrown. Buttons: nudge, reset, "Pop the stone" / "Put the stone back", pause, ¼ speed, show mesh; sliders for firmness and damping; readouts mass, volume %, grip %.

Rendering (WGSL): shadow map + top-down contact-AO map, scene pass (floor, stone, bubbles) with linear depth in alpha, back-face thickness pass, refracting jelly with Beer–Lambert absorption and scattering. Regions from rest-space SDFs: golden flesh; a ruby ring hugging the stone, broken up irregularly, with fine red fibres streaking out; the skin's blush bleeding a little way into the flesh. Skin: yellow with patchy red blush and pale flecks, a velvet sheen at grazing angles (nectarine: smooth and glossy). Stone: woody reddish-brown, dark furrows with shreds of red fibre, soft key shadows, low sheen. Varieties: Yellow, White, Nectarine. UI text in English.

summary.en: An interactive 3D gummy jellyfish built with WebGPU that can be grabbed, stretched, and squished in the browser, generated from a detailed prompt and compared against a version made by ChatGPT-6 Astra.

prompt.text:
Create “Jellyfish Jelly” — a beautiful, interactive 3D gummy jellyfish that users can grab, stretch, and squish directly in their browser. Deliver a complete single-file HTML experience using genuine WebGPU.
ART DIRECTION
Make it look like a premium translucent gummy sculpture:
A rounded, softly scalloped jellyfish bell.
Six flowing tentacles and a few delicate internal structures visible through the bell.

Glossy, translucent material with thickness-dependent color absorption, refraction, subtle subsurface lighting, and gentle rim highlights.
Rich color in thicker areas and more transparency at the edges.
A warm off-white background, soft studio lighting, and a subtle shadow beneath the floating jellyfish.
Keep the composition elegant and uncluttered. Avoid opaque plastic, excessive bloom, blown-out highlights, and visible mesh seams.
GEOMETRY AND PHYSICS
Generate all geometry procedurally. No external models or image files.
Use stable position-based dynamics or a mass-spring system with approximate volume preservation.
The bell should feel soft but substantial. Tentacles should be lighter, more flexible, and respond with slightly delayed motion. Their roots must remain attached to the bell.
Allow users to grab the bell or any tentacle at the clicked location. Pulling should deform the nearby area first, then elastically move the surrounding geometry.
On release, the jellyfish should wobble and gradually recover without snapping back, teleporting, or oscillating forever.
Add a subtle idle swimming motion: the bell slowly contracts and expands while the tentacles trail behind. Reduce this animation while the jellyfish is held.
Do not fake softness by scaling or rotating the entire model. Clamp extreme stretching and use fixed simulation steps.
INTERACTION
Left-click or touch to grab and stretch.

Right-drag or drag empty space to orbit the camera.
Support a limited zoom range.
Keep camera gestures separate from object interaction.
Include Give it a nudge, Reset, Pause, and Reset view.
Add Firmness, Internal damping, and Pulse rate sliders.
Include ¼ speed and Show mesh toggles.
Provide three palettes: Moon, Coral, and Deep. Switching colors must not reset the simulation.
INTERFACE
Use a minimal editorial layout with thin borders, generous whitespace, clean sans-serif controls, and a large italic serif heading:
“Jellyfish.”
Caption:
“A little current.
A little glow.
A very soft drifter.”
Place a compact “THE SPECIMEN” control panel on the right and a WebGPU status indicator at the top.
QUALITY AND PERFORMANCE
Reuse geometry and buffers instead of rebuilding meshes during dragging. Keep internal details attached to the deforming body.
Handle transparency carefully, without disappearing tentacles, flickering surfaces, or harsh black outlines.
Test repeated grabs, strong pulls, releases, palette changes, pause, reset, and mobile interaction. Show a clear fallback message if WebGPU is unavailable.
Deliver the full working HTML, not a mockup or code fragment.

title.zh: 浮空岛像素风F1赛车游戏
title.en: Pixel-art Formula 1 game on a floating island

summary.zh: Sonnet 5.5 用 Three.js 在单个 HTML 文件里做出的像素风 F1 游戏，赛道设在浮空岛上，有 12 辆车、雨天、进站、DRS 和自动驾驶模式。作者称耗时约 1.5 小时，API 费用 35.88 美元。
summary.en: A pixel-art Formula 1 game on a floating island with 12 cars, rain, pit stops, DRS and an autopilot mode, built by Sonnet 5.5 as a single HTML file with Three.js. The creator reports 1.5 hours of work and $35.88 in API costs.

prompt.text:
Build a single-file HTML5 game, "Island Grand Prix": a pixel-art 3D Formula 1 race on a floating voxel island. Use three.js r128 from cdnjs. No build step; everything inline (HTML, CSS, JS). The page <title> is a 2-4 word name.

LOOK
- Render the 3D scene to a low-res render target (default 2 px art pixels, slider 1-6). Then a post pass: depth-texture outlines wherever depth jumps, snap every pixel to a fixed 90-colour palette in OKLab, Bayer 4x4 ordered dither. Orthographic isometric camera (rotate, zoom, tilt, pixel-snapped target). Place the camera ~850 m from its target with far plane ~1700 so the 660 m wide island is never clipped at low tilt angles. Sun shadow map, day / dusk / night lighting that eases between states, six floodlight towers with point lights, rain particles.
- Island: a slab of 2.4 m voxel columns (ellipse ~330 x 232 m with a lobed outline), terraced at the rim, banded soil and slate strata below, a waterfall, floating rocks and cones underneath. Build cells for the WHOLE island, including the core, and give the slab material side = DoubleSide so no sky shows through the underside from any angle. The top plane carries a 2048 px painted ground canvas: grass, mowed run-off strips, paddock tarmac, plaza tiles, lake, harbour basin, town streets, stream.
- Circuit: a closed centripetal Catmull-Rom spline through ~24 control points, ~1240 m long, resampled every 1 m with tangent, normal and smoothed curvature. Meshes: 14 m asphalt ribbon, red/white kerbs on corners, gravel traps, start line, 14 grid boxes, barriers, sponsor boards, instanced tyre walls, marshal posts with little marshals. Pit lane with entry/exit ramps, six garages (coloured parapet, skylights, air-con, mast, team flag), pit wall with signal gantry and screens, control tower.
- Venue: 216 m main stand with a giant screen, ~9 corner stands with instanced coloured crowds that cheer, start gantry with five lamp pairs, podium, lake with lighthouse islet and yachts, harbour crane, small town with windmill, ferris wheel, fan zone, paddock motorhomes, helipad + helicopter, gate arch, blimp, balloon, birds.
- Doll's-house lift: every tall structure (each stand, each garage bay, towers, tower of control ...) is its own lift group with a bounding box. Each frame, cast the sight line from the camera target toward the camera; groups whose box it crosses below roof height rise 90 m and stop casting shadows (hide when fully raised). Switch the effect off in the Island camera and by checkbox. Merge static meshes by material; instance crowds and trees; aim for ~1,000-1,300 draw calls.

GAME
- 12 cars, 6 invented teams x 2 drivers, procedurally named. Cars are boxes: monocoque, sidepods, front and rear wings with a flap that opens for DRS, helmet, number plate, four wheels with steering fronts, coloured tyre-compound discs, brake light.
- Flow: grid -> five red lights with a random hold -> race -> chequered flag -> finish -> podium ceremony. Formats: Quick 3, Short 5, Full 10 laps. Count the line crossing at the start as the start, not a lap; guard lap counting with unwrapped distance.
- Track model: per-sample speed profile from curvature (grip G0 ~25 m/s2, acceleration ~16, braking ~40, vmax ~74 m/s) with a forward and a backward pass.
- AI cars run on rails (distance s along the spline, lateral offset): speed from the profile, racing line, pass offsets and speed caps when a car is ahead, DRS, tyre wear per compound, pit stops when worn or when the weather mismatches the tyres, rare random retirements (likelier in rain), per-race pace jitter.
- Player car: arcade physics (steering rate falls with speed; lateral grip = G0 x downforce x tyre x surface; slide and smoke when over the limit; gravel and grass drag; wall hits with sparks; DRS +6% on straights within range; engine modes lean / standard / push). Autopilot is ON by default: the player's car is driven like the AI (and pits itself when the tyres are worn). Any drive key (arrows, WASD, Space) or touch on the pad takes the wheel instantly; the key G, a corner button ("Autopilot / You drive") and a checkbox hand it back. An automatic "marshals push you back" recovery when stuck in gravel.
- Cars are solid: after every step resolve overlaps for all pairs in track coordinates (car 4.9 x 2.2 m): the rear car is moved back and slowed to the front car's speed, side-by-side cars move apart; skip cars in the pit lane; add sparks and a bump sound on hard contact.
- Pit stop: box call -> pit-lane entry with a 22 m/s limiter -> stop at the team's garage -> crew animation (jack, wheel guns, lollipop) -> tyre change -> release and merge back onto the track before handing control back.
- Conditions: Dry / Damp / Wet change grip, wear, visibility, light and rain; starting tyres switch to inter/wet automatically.

UI (panel beside the canvas, below it on phones)
- On the canvas: timing tower (compact on phones), speedometer strip (speed, gear, lap, tyre with wear, DRS state, position and gap), caption banners, autopilot button top right.
- Panel: format, team and driver, rival strength, new race, skip grid, speed 1/2x-4x, pause, auto-next, track condition with grip/wear/visibility gauges, time of day with floodlights, tyres for start and next stop, engine mode, box this lap, back on track, camera (Follow / Chase / Heli / Island), rotate, zoom, pixel size, outline / dither / raw 3D / sound / lift toggles, classification table, stats, race log, palette view. Set the initial camera mode explicitly so it matches the pressed button.
- Keys: arrows/WASD drive, Space DRS, G autopilot, B box, M engine, T next tyres, R back on track, C track condition, L light, Q/E turn, 1-4 cameras, +/- zoom, P pause, N new race, K skip grid. Touch: dock a left/right + DRS/brake/throttle pad under the canvas; drag to turn, pinch to zoom. Procedural WebAudio engine note, beeps, horn, pit gun.

QUALITY BAR
- Headless bot tests: AI laps ~25 s, a simple bot ~27 s, full races finish in dry, damp and wet, pit stops happen on 10-lap races, zero car overlaps, no console errors, no horizontal scroll on a phone.

title.zh: 电影感2D分镜短片《雨站》

summary.zh: 这条30秒风格化2D分镜短片《雨站》由 Opus 5.5 调用 GPT Image 画原画、Real-ESRGAN 超分、Depth Anything 估深度，再用自写的 Python+ffmpeg 渲染器合成画面和声音输出，作者贴出了完整的长提示词。
summary.en: A stylised 30-second 2D animatic ('Rain Station') made by Opus 5.5 with GPT Image art, Real-ESRGAN/Depth Anything, and a custom Python+ffmpeg renderer, from a long structured prompt pasted in full.

prompt.text:
帮我做一条 30 秒的 2D 动画分镜预演短片《雨站》，要标杆级画质。不装 HyperFrames/Remotion，全部自己写代码（Python + ffmpeg）完成。

故事（24fps，2.39:1，4K）：雨夜高架站台。她穿米色风衣、撑透明伞，站在近侧站台；对面路灯下站着他，穿深灰长大衣、围围巾。
1. 0–6.4s 透明伞雨珠特写 → 后拉，焦点移到对面露出他（过肩镜头）
2. 6.4–9.4s 他的中近景：低头 → 抬头看向画左
3. 9.4–12.4s 她的正面近景：眨眼 → 认出他；远处传来鸣笛
4. 12.4–17s 远景：车头灯光先到，5 节列车驶过；第一个车厢缝隙里他还在，第二个已经空了
5. 17–18.8s 她含泪的近景，车窗光带扫过她的脸，头发被风吹起
6. 18.8–22.4s 尾灯远去，对面站台空了；他那盏灯闪几下后熄灭
7. 22.4–28.6s 她的背影，焦点从空站台拉回她；身后脚步声，一把黑伞遮到她头顶，她回头看向镜头；男声“好久不见。”，配字幕
8. 28.6–30s 黑场片名“雨站 / RAIN STATION”

做法：
- 原画：用GPT Image 2.5 画远景、他、她、列车（头车/中车/尾车）。人物一律用纯绿 #00FF00 背景，自己抠像（带参考图要透明背景会得到假棋盘格）。同一角色的各个姿态放在同一个会话里，以基准图为参考连续编辑；换姿态时只合成变化的区域。
- 画质：用 Real-ESRGAN x4plus anime 6B（HF 上的 safetensors 版，自己写 RRDBNet，跑在 MPS 上）把全部原画放大 4 倍；用 Depth Anything V2 估算远景深度，做逐像素视差。
- 渲染：自己写 2.5D 合成器。各层按真实深度摆放，针孔相机按真实焦距运动；做圆形焦外光斑、焦点转移、3D 雨丝、列车运动模糊、体积光、泛光和胶片光晕、细颗粒、调色。人物用网格变形做呼吸、风吹发梢、伞抖，关键姿态按日式“一拍二”切换。4K 超采样，逐帧缓存到磁盘，分 3 个进程按时间段并行（16GB 内存）。
- 声音：Mixkit 真实音效（雨、伞面雨声、列车、鸣笛、脚步）；按剧情节点写谱，用 Logic/GarageBand 自带的施坦威钢琴和弦乐采样渲染；台词用 Kokoro 中文男声；按镜头做声音远近，响度 -16 LUFS。
- 每一步都渲染预览帧、拼成图自检，修好再出片。交付 4K 母版和 1080p 分享版。

title.zh: 纯代码UI动效循环动画

summary.zh: 一段完全用代码渲染而非After Effects制作的UI动态设计循环视频，基于作者公开的Claude Opus 5.5结构化提示模板（规定UI状态、弹簧动画和节拍同步剪辑），使用Playwright和ffmpeg渲染。
summary.en: A looping UI motion design video rendered entirely in code (no After Effects) using Claude Opus 5.5, built from an open-sourced structured prompt template specifying UI states, spring animations and beat-synced edits, rendered with Playwright and ffmpeg.

prompt.text:
<inputs>
Ask me for: 8 to 12 UI states I want the shape to transform into (e.g. button, loader, player, slider, toggle, tabs, chart, command palette, toast), pure black and white or one accent color, and a royalty-free song around 120 BPM (e.g. Mixkit, free for commercial use).
</inputs>

<direction>
Dribbble-level UI motion. One shape, no cuts: every state is the same element morphing its size, radius and color while its content swaps with a quick blur.
A cursor controls every change with real clicks and drags. Light warm-gray canvas, black and white components, one clean UI font (Geist).
Springs everywhere, with only a tiny overshoot. The camera zooms so each state fills the entire frame. The last frame matches the first frame, so it loops perfectly.
Banned: bouncy easing, particle bursts, glows, gradients on UI chrome, mismatched icon strokes, dead time, anything that looks like a template.
</direction>

<structure>
120 BPM, 7 bars, something happens on every beat.
Button → loader → check → dynamic island → music player with a play/pause morph → scrub the progress bar → it becomes a volume slider that stretches when dragged past max → a toggle flips on the beat → the knob becomes a liquid tab indicator → the tabs expand into a chart that draws itself, with a tooltip on hover → it collapses into ⌘K → type to filter → enter → toast → back to the button.
</structure>

<build>
One HTML file, square 1440x1440. Every style is calculated from time inside seek(t): no CSS transitions, no timers, no state carried between frames.
Springs use closed-form step responses. A value that changes targets multiple times is the sum of one spring per change, so it remains a pure function of time.
The tab indicator's two edges follow different springs, so the leading edge stretches ahead of the trailing one. Use the same trick for the toggle knob.
Drags use direct manipulation: while the cursor is held, the value is calculated from its position. On release it springs back from wherever it was.
Analyze the song with numpy to find the beat grid and start on a downbeat. Position every UI sound by its measured peak.
Render with Playwright: 4 subframes per frame, blended with ffmpeg tmix for motion blur at 60fps.
Render one frame per beat before the full render. Fix anything off the grid, cramped or difficult to read.
</build>

<gotchas>
Never put will-change on anything the camera scales or the text becomes blurry.
Text that swaps inside a morphing container needs its own enter and exit timing or it overlaps.
Make the final frame identical to the first, including cursor position and speed, or the loop stutters.
</gotchas>

<start>
Ask me for the inputs, then show me the state list on the beat grid before writing any code.
</start>

title.zh: 嵌套旋转六边形弹球物理模拟
title.en: Nested spinning hexagon ball physics simulation

summary.zh: 一个由Claude Opus 5.5根据详细提示词生成的自包含HTML/Three.js物理模拟，展示球体在相互反向旋转的多层六边形笼子中弹跳，带有卡通渲染风格、可破碎墙体和基于Web Audio的生成式音效。
summary.en: A physics simulation of balls bouncing inside nested, oppositely spinning hexagonal prisms with cel-shaded visuals, breakable walls and generative Web Audio sound, built as a self-contained HTML/Three.js file using Claude Opus 5.5 from a detailed prompt.

prompt.text:
Build a single self-contained HTML file (Three.js via CDN, no other assets) that is the 2026 version of the "ball bouncing inside a spinning hexagon" test.

Scene: a large hollow hexagonal prism (a 3D hexagon) slowly spinning on two axes at once. Inside it, a smaller hexagonal prism spins the opposite way, and inside that, a tiny one. Three nested spinning cages. The cage walls are see-through panels drawn only as clean outlines with a very light flat tint, so every ball inside stays clearly visible.

Physics (write your own, no physics library):
- Start with 1 ball inside the innermost cage. Every 2 seconds a new ball spawns, up to 300, each with its own random size, mass and color.
- Real gravity, friction, restitution and spin. Balls must collide with each other and with the rotating walls, picking up the wall's velocity at the contact point so they get flung realistically. No tunneling through walls, no jitter when balls rest on each other.
- When a ball hits a wall hard enough, that wall panel cracks and eventually breaks into flat shards that also obey physics, so balls can escape into the next cage outward.
- The outer cage never breaks. Escaped balls pile up at the bottom of it.

Look, clean cel-shaded style:
- Toon shading on everything: 2 or 3 hard shading bands per object, crisp dark outlines (inverted-hull or edge detection), flat colors from a small tasteful palette.
- A plain flat light background (soft off-white or pale gray), with a simple flat floor shadow under the cage.
- No bloom, no glow, no neon, no lens flares, no motion blur, no particle haze, no gradients, no transparency stacking. No visual artifacts: no z-fighting, no flickering outlines, no shadow acne, no aliasing (use antialiasing and a sensible pixel ratio).
- Impacts get small, flat cartoon "pop" marks that vanish quickly, not sparks.
- It should look like a clean animated illustration, not a tech demo.

Camera: a slow, smooth orbit by default, plus drag to orbit and scroll to zoom.

Sound: synthesize everything with the Web Audio API. Each collision makes a soft pitched tone based on ball size and impact speed, so it turns into gentle generative music as it gets chaotic. Breaking panels get their own sound. Keep it quiet and pleasant, never clipping.

UI: a small, minimal flat panel in the corner (no glassmorphism) with sliders for gravity, spin speed, bounciness and ball count, a "slow motion" toggle, a "reset" button, and an FPS counter. It must stay at 60fps with 300 balls on a laptop.

summary.en: A 78-second anime fight was built in Three.js with code-only rendering, six parallel agent departments, and an orchestral score. The creator says it used no image or video generation models, After Effects, or Blender.

prompt.text:
Create a 2D anime short. It must look completely like real Japanese anime, as if it were taken directly from a finished theatrical anime film. This is traditional-looking, hand-drawn 2D anime, not a 3D animation, a moving illustration, or a stylized web graphic.

Build everything in three.js (WebGL2) in the browser, render every frame headless in Chrome with a painted-background brush pass and an ink pass, and encode with ffmpeg. Deliver one 1920x1080, 24 fps MP4 with an orchestral soundtrack. Use any tools, libraries, references, guides, literally anything, as long as the final result looks 100% like hand-drawn 2D anime.

REFERENCE
Retell the final fight and the Serious Punch from episode 12 of One Punch Man shot for shot: the same actions, staging, camera angles, lens feel and timing. Redesign every visual from scratch, so the scene is recognisable only by what happens, never by how anything looks. 78 seconds, 31 shots.

WORLD
A shining city on a ring around a planet: towers of white coral with coral, apricot and celadon accents, hanging gardens, a pale esplanade with a balustrade, and a sea of clouds far below. Above the north of the city hangs a 7 km hive ship with ribs like a whale skeleton.

CHARACTERS
The hero is a calm capybara janitor in overalls with a straw broom and a small citrus on his head. The villain is an insect warlord in wine-coloured armour set with gems, who sheds that armour for a mantle of lime energy.

STORY
A quiet morning. The capybara sweeps one small pile of leaves while a lime beam cuts a trench through the district behind him, and he does not notice. A sky-tram pod plants itself beside him. The hive ship arrives. The warlord lands, boasts, and is ignored; the broom taps its toe. One slash cuts the skyline on a single straight line. The armour bursts. A barrage, a rush, a blade strike: the esplanade becomes a crater and he is left on a pillar, black with soot, yawning. He flicks the warlord apart, it regrows, rises and drains the sky into a spiral around a star. The wind finally takes his pile and the citrus falls from his head. For the first time in the film he looks up. One sweep of the broom: the sky is hollowed out, the ship breaks and the clouds open around the whole planet. The last leaf lands. He goes back to work.

LIGHT
Every shot has its own light rig: key, rim, bounce and one energy light with a visible source. High-key noon, ochre dust after the landing, a drained indigo sky under the star, then the cleanest air of the film. Impact frames in negative, white and ink with lime. Textures at several scales that fade with distance.

MOTION
Living bodies move with weight: centre of mass over the feet, no foot sliding, anticipation, overshoot, arcs, breathing, characters animated on twos.

SOUND
Real orchestral samples (CC0), mood decided second by second: a calm morning, dread when the ship arrives, minor brass and percussion through the fight with every hit on picture, total silence before the sweep, and the first major chord of the film only after it.

TEAM
Parallel agent departments, each owning its own files: city, sky, warlord, capybara, FX, sound. A shared map and shot list keep them in sync.

CHECKS
Before the final render a script tests every frame on the real geometry with BVH: no character, hand or foot inside the ground, props or another body; the camera never enters a mesh or goes below ground; feet do not slide; no camera jerks; nothing appears or vanishes in the middle of a shot.

summary.zh: 作者用同一段提示词让 Sonnet 5.5、Opus 5.5、GPT-6 Astra 和 GPT-6.1 Sol 分别制作浮空岛露天泳池的像素风 Three.js 3D 场景，并列出了各模型的耗时和费用。
summary.en: A comparison of a pixel-art 3D Three.js scene of an open-air lido on a floating island, built from the same prompt by Sonnet 5.5, Opus 5.5, GPT-6 Astra and GPT-6.1 Sol, with time and cost listed for each model.

prompt.text:
Build "Deep End": an open-air lido on a floating island of earth and rock, rendered as a real-time 3D scene in pixel art (three.js, orthographic isometric camera rendering into a small low-res target, no anti-aliasing, depth-buffer outlines, every pixel snapped to a fixed 64-colour palette matched in OKLab; quarter-turn rotation, zoom, pixel-size slider, Raw 3D toggle).
Scene: a 25 m lap pool and a 5 m deep diving pool cut into a concrete deck; 1 m and 3 m springboards that visibly bend; a 1930s concrete diving tower with platforms at 5, 7.5 and 10 m and an open stair; striped changing cabins with a clock, a kiosk, loungers and parasols; a judges' table.
Diving meet with real physics: each dive is flown, not animated — takeoff speed and angular momentum are solved to land the somersaults, angular momentum is conserved so tucking spins the diver faster and kicking out slows them to line up the entry. Divers kick out slightly early or late (more on harder dives), the entry angle sets the splash, five judges hold up score cards, highest and lowest are dropped, the rest are multiplied by the degree of difficulty. Events: 10 m, 3 m, free swim.
Water: each pool surface is a wave-equation height field (~20 cm cells) — entries, strokes, rain and clicks make rings that bounce off the walls; shaded from its normals with sun glints and a mirrored reflection of the lido; caustics on the tiled floor.
People: box-rig figures with two-bone IK — swimmers doing freestyle, breaststroke and backstroke with flip turns; divers swim to the ladder, shower, sit in the warm tub and climb again; children who run and get whistled at by the lifeguard; wet footprints on the deck that dry in the sun.
Light and weather: day / dusk / night (pool lights glow underwater, tower floodlights at night), dry / rain (rain rings the water and darkens the deck). Click the water to make a splash. Side panel with the meet scoreboard, controls and a short "How it's drawn" note. Original fictional content only, English UI.

summary.zh: 作者分享了用 Opus 5.5 制作可直接用于游戏的 3D 角色的流程。先把概念设定图切成多个视角，用 Tripo 生成模型，再通过 Claude Code 编写 Python 脚本在 Blender 中完成绑骨和动画，最后用于一款 Unity 网页游戏。
summary.en: A workflow for making game-ready 3D characters with Opus 5.5. A concept sheet is split into views, turned into a model in Tripo, rigged and animated in Blender through Python scripts in Claude Code, and used in a Unity browser game.

prompt.text:
rig model.glb for animation. run blender headless with python scripts only and save every script so you can rerun it
1. apply all transforms, merge duplicate verts, scale to [height] m, feet on the floor
2. render orthographic front and side views with a grid, open them and write the joint positions (hips, spine, neck, head, shoulders, elbows, wrists, knees, ankles) to joints.json
3. build the armature on those joints. long cloth below the hips (cape, coat skirt) gets 2 bones of its own, front and back, children of the hips
4. bind with automatic weights, then fix them with rules in code: torso, collar, scarf and coat get 0 on the arm bones, the head bone moves only the head and hair, belt and pouches go 100% on the hips, the skirt goes on the cape bones, max 4 bones per vertex, normalize
5. pose test: arms up 90, arms forward 60, a step with each leg, a head turn. render each pose front and side, open the renders, list every spot where the mesh tears or stretches, fix the weights there and render again, max 3 rounds
6. export fbx
